# 1.2.77 - a voice tile in place of the camera dock, and a smaller room tile

One stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E78, the owner's request A9), released alone as an ordinary release: every screen with LiveKit
voice shows a voice tile at the right wall - who you hear speaking in your own voice room, a microphone button and a speaker
button with the list "Who you hear" - and Foundry's camera dock leaves the screen while its sound keeps playing; the gear gets a
Voice section. The room tile is smaller under Monokuma Legacy and beside the notices, and the owner's three reports on 1.2.76 are
fixed. Most of it was measured in the headless harness on a stand-in for LiveKit, the screen's layout also in Chromium on the
glass harness, some only read in the code; none of it was tried in a real Foundry, with a real LiveKit server or at a table.

## Before installing

1. **The camera dock leaves the screen.** While the voice tile is on (the default), Foundry's camera dock and its pop-out windows
   are not shown on any screen, a GM's included. They stay in the page, because LiveKit plays everybody's sound through them, so
   the sound keeps playing (read in the code; that it still plays after a reload at a real table is LIVE-E78-10, not tried yet).
   The camera pictures, the connection quality, the pop-outs, a GM's own camera preview and any buttons another module puts in
   the dock (proximity-voice-chat's among them) go with it. There is no tile, and the dock is Foundry's as before, when
   avclient-livekit is not active or the world's A/V mode is off or video only (read in the code).
2. **The way back.** The world setting **Voice tile instead of the camera dock**, in the module's settings, is on by default and
   is a GM's to change. Off brings Foundry's camera dock back for everyone and takes the tile away, on every screen as the
   setting changes, with no reload (measured on the stand-in, scenario 75 A and D; at a table: LIVE-E78-10).
3. **What a player reaches with the dock hidden.** Their own microphone, on the tile; the speaker's list **Who you hear**, with
   a volume and **Mute *name* for you** for each person, only on their screen; and the gear's **Voice** section: microphone,
   sound output, the microphone's mode and the push-to-talk key. The microphone, a volume, a device and the mode were each
   reached as a player in scenario 75 with the dock hidden and written to that player's own settings (real devices:
   LIVE-E78-04). Only a GM has, in the list, **Block *name*'s microphone for everyone**: the GM handbook calls it Foundry's own
   block, the dock's, disabled with the reason while the game holds that microphone - today for a death the GMs keep secret,
   which a block would tell the table (at a real table: LIVE-E78-03, LIVE-E78-06).
4. **A GM's microphone is no longer turned on** when the GM walks their Monokuma into a room. The module mutes and unmutes nobody
   on its own: use the microphone on the tile.
5. **Set the world's A/V mode to audio only.** The tile shows no video. While the world is in audio and video and the tile stands
   in for the dock, Season Setup's **Pre-season checks** add a Voice line: "This world sends video nobody watches: set the A/V
   mode to audio only."
6. **The room tile is smaller** in two places (the glass harness in Chromium, the tile's box). Under Monokuma Legacy, under the
   clock: 430x364 at 1920x1080 and 430x310 at 1366x768, where 1.2.76 drew 430x491 at both. Under Stained Glass beside the
   notices its pane still runs to the screen's bottom edge, with no plain glass under it: at 1366x768 the box is 301x129
   (301x376 in 1.2.76) on a pane of 344x202 that leans 6 degrees and shows 185 px above the edge at its middle, at 1366x657 and
   lower 301x122 on 344x195, also leaning, and at the five other sizes where it stands there (1224x768, 1300x768, 1264x800,
   1280x800, 1280x720) 301x122 to 301x134 on a pane of 325x163 to 325x175 that does not lean. Opened, its description scrolls
   inside the tile (2.4 lines show at 1366x768, 2.1 at 1280x720). Stained Glass's tile under the clock is unchanged: 265x364
   at 1920x1080, as in 1.2.76.
7. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back. **On The Forge, install from this
   release's manifest URL.** Pictures from your Assets Library are now taken for rooms in Room Setup and for voice portraits (see
   "Smaller fixes"; not tried on The Forge yet: LIVE-E78-11).
8. **Settings, keys and texts.** Two new settings (127 registered, 125 at 1.2.76): the world switch above, and `voicePeerMutes`,
   hidden and per browser, which keeps who each person muted for themselves. One new keybinding, **Mute or unmute your
   microphone**, with no key bound (bind one in Foundry's Controls). `lang/en.json` goes from 3374 to 3416 strings (42 added, none
   removed, 2 reworded) and `lang/pl.json` from 4145 to 4191 (46 added, none removed, 2 reworded). For a GM, among others: the
   setting, the Pre-season checks line above, the block's two reasons ("You cannot block this microphone now." and "This death is
   still a secret: a block would give it away.") and Room Setup's refusal, now "{room}: the picture was not saved. Pick a jpg,
   png, webp or avif from this game's files, or on The Forge from your Assets Library.", with the Description tab's note to
   match. The handbooks were updated; the Foundry and Daggerheart versions in the manifest are unchanged.

## At the table

### The voice tile and its buttons

- **Where it stands.** Under Stained Glass, a pane of the glass at the right wall under the Projects tray, with no glass to its
  left, the microphone over the speaker at its top right corner (their centres 20 and 25 px from the wall, 19 and 24 at 2560x1440
  and 3840x2160). On the glass harness in Chromium it stands at the wall at every desk size of the sweep, GM and player: 194x281
  at 1920x1080 and 1920x1200, 258x374 at 2560x1440 and 3840x2160, and 181 wide and 151 to 262 high on the other desks that are
  not short (a player's 181x262 and a GM's 181x225 at 1366x768). The list opens inside the screen and cuts nothing, and the
  caption's brush is the game state's colour, at every size of the sweep. Under Monokuma Legacy it stands at the right edge over
  the corner's buttons, 163x188 at every desk size of the sweep, GM and player.
- **On a short screen** (in the sweep a GM's at 1366x657 and lower, a player's at 1366x600 and lower) the tile is one row: the
  name, cut short when long, and both buttons, the speaker with its number; it is never lower than the buttons.
- **What it shows.** The portrait across the tile and the name on the **Speaking** plate of whoever you hear speaking in your own
  voice room, never anybody outside it; a player is shown under a character they own, else under their account's name. A new
  speaker takes the tile after a quarter of a second of speech; when they stop, the next speaker takes over at once, or the
  portrait stays a second and a half and fades (at once with reduced motion); then only the two buttons stay. Someone who leaves
  your room, a lost connection or a new room clears it at once (on the stand-in for LiveKit; real speech: LIVE-E78-10).
- **The microphone** mutes and unmutes your own microphone and nobody else's; a key does the same once you bind one. Struck
  through, you muted it; with a small lock, "The GM blocked your microphone."; grey and struck through, the game holds it, during
  an Eclipse, with the reason under it, and a click changes nothing and says why. A small dot means "You are not connected to
  voice." or "Voice is in its own window - use the controls there."; with push to talk it wears **PTT**. A Monocub keeps its
  microphone in an Eclipse and is told "Eclipse: nobody hears you until the lights come back." (LIVE-E78-02, LIVE-E78-09).
  It lights up while your microphone carries your voice: its rim in the game's colour under Stained Glass, a bone ring under
  Monokuma Legacy (colours read in the code; the lighting measured on the stand-in for LiveKit, not seen with a real one).
- **The speaker** shows, without a click, how many others are in your voice room - everybody who can hear you, silent or
  speaking, named or not - and opens **Who you hear**. It is struck through while **Mute everybody for you** is on.
- **On a stacked screen** the voice tile is a part of the tiles' row, beside the room tile: 236x44 under Stained Glass and
  300x44 under Monokuma Legacy at all seven stacked sizes of the glass sweep in Chromium, GM and player. A small portrait, the
  name of who speaks, and the microphone and the speaker with its number (read in the code; a real phone: LIVE-E78-05).

### Who you hear, the GM's block and the gear's Voice section

- **The list** has a row for each person in your voice room whom the game can name, by name, with their portrait, a dot while
  they speak, a volume slider and **Mute *name* for you** (then **Hear *name* again**); at the top **Mute everybody for you**.
  These are yours alone: nobody else hears the difference. With nobody else there the list says "Nobody else is in your
  channel." Escape closes it. Read in the code only: moving the slider of someone muted for you unmutes them at that volume;
  someone you hid earlier in the camera dock reads "Hidden earlier in the camera dock: you do not hear them." with **Show and
  listen**; a click outside closes the list. A volume and a mute were measured to stay when the voice room reconnects; after a
  reload at a table they are LIVE-E78-03.
- **The GM's block.** A GM's list has **Block *name*'s microphone for everyone** (then **Unblock *name*'s microphone**) on each
  row. It is disabled with "This death is still a secret: a block would give it away." for a death the GMs keep, and it never
  lifts a hold of the game's. The blocked player's microphone shows the lock.
- **The gear's Voice section.** Where the world has voice, the gear's window has a **Voice** section: **Microphone**, **Sound
  output**, **Microphone mode** (**Always on** or **Push to talk**) and the push-to-talk key with **Change the key**. If no
  microphone is listed: "Allow the browser to use your microphone, then open this window again to choose one." Against real
  devices: LIVE-E78-04.

### Smaller fixes

- **The Forge's pictures.** On The Forge, Room Setup keeps a jpg, png, webp or avif picked from your Assets Library, and the room
  tile shows it; a voice portrait from there shows on the voice tile and in the list (the character's picture first, else the
  account's avatar). Off The Forge nothing changed. Measured on a stand-in for The Forge, not on The Forge (LIVE-E78-11).
- **The Still to act strip.** The strip and the other leaning blocks under Stained Glass stand still on an idle screen: in
  Chromium, GM and player, idle for 5 s, 4 passes at 1920x1080 and 5 at 1366x768 before the fix, 0 at every desk size after
  (LIVE-E78-12).
- **The anvil.** The Foundry tools button above the book wears a white pixel anvil, in both themes; no Foundry logo is drawn in
  the corner (R548 reads the colour and the missing logo; LIVE-E78-13).

## Changed

- New files: `scripts/voice-tile.mjs` (the tile, its buttons, the list, the body class `drpg-dock-hidden`),
  `scripts/voice-panel.mjs` (the gear's section) and `audit/harness/lib/livekit.mjs` (a LiveKit Room for the harness). voice.mjs
  gains `voiceRowFor`, `micHold` and `moduleHoldsMic`, and `reconcileNow` no longer calls `toggleAudio`; camera-view.mjs gains
  `voiceIdentity`, `voiceActorFor` takes a player's character only when they own it, and `rtcSettingsChanged` replaces the
  `collapseCameraViews` hook. The tile reads avclient-livekit's Room and the dock's own elements, never `settings.activity`.
- glass.mjs: the `voice-block` and its pane (`voicePlacement`, `settleVoice`, `seatVoiceArt`), `roomCapH`, `roomNotesH`, and
  `OVERHANG` with `railOverhang`, so a pass over the same geometry writes the rotation sheet zero times. utils.mjs `forgeAsset`,
  read by `safeRoomImage` and the notice history; the launcher's face masked with `--drpg-px-anvil`. `relay-guard.mjs`,
  `gm-bridge.mjs` and `module.json` are unchanged.
- **New tests:** 20 numbered ones, R533 to R552 (4 in tier 0: R533, R534, R544, R552; 16 in tier 1), and scenario
  75-voice-tile in the ci set (26, 25 at 1.2.76). Among the older ones R432, R509 and R512 were changed, and scenario 74 gained
  phase K. The skip baseline goes from 22 to 23 rows (R543: a browser's layout). Next free: R553. `known-leaks.json` gains A9-K3.
  `audit/glass-sweep.mjs` reads the voice tile, pins the room tile's box, pane and tilt per size, and reads an idle screen.
- Round 2: glass.mjs `VOICE_MIN` (42), `VOICE_FULL` (114; under it `data-fit="compact"`), `--drpg-voice-lift`, `roomNotesLift`
  and a four-argument `roomNotesH`; utils.mjs `forgeAsset` reads the name `ForgeVTT` in a `try` (a class or a property);
  voice-tile.mjs `paintSelf` (`.is-speaking`). The glass harness reads the tile's parts, list and brush; the sweep adds 1366x600,
  1366x560, `PIN_CORNER` and the Legacy tile; 75 D reads the cut signature, 75 E the tile. AUDIT item 213 is now LIVE-E78-13.

## Known gaps

- Seventy-two live checks stand open (items 163 to 235 of the audit's section 9.2 but 213, now LIVE-E78-13): 59 of 1.2.76's
  sixty and LIVE-E78-01 to -13: the P11 matrix, the room picture past the screen's edge, the voice buttons at the corner, the
  hidden dock and Foundry v14's real camera pop-out id (-01); the microphone's states, avclient-livekit muting the microphone
  itself on the module's mute, push to talk included (-02); the list, the block and a mute after a reload (-03); real devices
  (-04); a real phone (-05); Foundry's server on a block sent from a player's browser, and the blocked player's own browser
  (-06); a lost connection and avclient-livekit's private API at a table's version (-07); proximity-voice-chat, which can zero
  volumes so the tile shows nobody (-08); voice in its own window (-09); the owner's two-browser test T1, a table check and not
  a condition of this release (-10); The Forge's Assets Library and its object read in the console (-11); the idle strip (-12);
  the anvil (-13).
- **A known leak (A9-K3), closed by E19 (planned for 1.2.82, a plan).** A character killed in secret moves to the main voice
  room at the kill, not at the discovery: players there see the name in **Who you hear** and its count grow before anybody has
  found the body, and see the victim on the tile when they speak; by reading, the count falls in the room the victim left.
  Foundry's camera dock showed the same in 1.2.76 (by reading). Scenario 75 reproduces it, the tile included, and counts it as
  expected.
- Read in the code, not measured: avclient-livekit's private API and where it draws a person's sound, as the design read 0.6.8;
  that `display: none !important` wins over Foundry's own dock rules; the names of Foundry's `rtcSettingsChanged` hook and of a
  user's `canBroadcastAudio` (without it the lock never shows); whether Foundry's server lets a player point their account at a
  character they do not own (the tile no longer shows one); the order in which LiveKit reports a participant gone.
- Not measured: the buttons repainting on a real change of a user's permission; the speaker's number as a browser draws it on the
  tile and in the stacked row; a real participant LiveKit maps to nobody; whether a player can set their own avatar in Foundry
  v14. While voice reconnects the tile keeps the last speaker. The hidden dock still receives video while the world sends it.
- On The Forge a voice portrait may be any picture on The Forge's asset host (the GM handbook says so). The path The Forge's
  picker writes, and whether The Forge's own object is a property or a class (the module reads both), were not read at The Forge.
- A GM's desk 1366 wide under 546 px high is not kept (read at r2-H1: at 1366x544 the voice pane meets the corner's); a name
  over about 44 letters ran under the buttons just over the compact height at r2-H1, not read since r2-H3 moved them. The
  buttons' glyphs, the compact tile and your microphone's ring were not seen at a table, nor the ring with a real LiveKit, and
  no live check names the compact tile or the ring.
- The room description's chevron was not clicked in the glass harness, which opens the description by unhiding it.

## Checked

- The headless suite and the ci scenarios, run as `npm test` runs them, on this release's code (commit 3ad0ca0: the tree that
  ships but for the version stamps, these notes, the stage registry's rows and the local gate's record): 1338 passed, 0
  failed, 23 skipped (1.2.76: 1319, 0 and 22). The scenarios: 26 of 26 green; 72's three expected reds stand (S17-31 until
  E43, a Foundry limit, S17-64 until E60) and 75's one (A9-K3 until E19); scenario 01, the suite run from the harness, 20 of
  20. The skip baseline has 23 rows (22 at 1.2.76; the new one, R543, needs a browser's layout). The lint and the Polish
  file's prose check (497 of 497 strings covered) were green in the same run and on every commit's fast set.
- The first release run (Actions run 38557127125, 14.10) stopped in the suite at 1337 passed, 1 failed, 23 skipped. The one
  test timed the GM's 400 ms second look for a roll record on `Date.now`, the wall clock, and read it short; by how much the
  run did not record. Node's timer runs on the monotonic clock, cut to the millisecond, and the wall clock can also be
  stepped mid-wait. On Node 22.22.2 here, 52 to 65 of 3000 short timeouts read one millisecond short on `Date.now` and none
  of 1500 400 ms ones did. The test now times the wait on `performance.now`, Node's monotonic clock, and takes 399 ms; the
  code it tests did not change.
- The glass sweep, `node audit/glass-sweep.mjs`, in Chromium, both themes and both roles:
  on 3ad0ca0, the code that ships, at its 25 sizes (1366x600 and 1366x560 new): green, 46 lines with glass, 0 failing, the
  curtain's self-check 0 on each, every pin held (the room tile's place, box and lean, the voice buttons at the corner), the
  room pane beside the notices 344x202 over the screen's foot with no plain pane under it at 1366x768, the voice tile whole
  with its name, its buttons and the caption in the game state's colour on every Stained Glass desk line and 163x188 under
  Monokuma Legacy, the list opened inside the screen with no cut, and each control it plants seen.
  HF2's whole sweep (5250087) read its 32 idle lines at 0 passes. r1-G3's sweep of the seven sizes beside the notices, both
  roles: green, every pin and the tilt pin held. On a stand-in for Foundry's sidebar, without Foundry's sheets, Font Awesome or
  LiveKit.
- The handoffs record the mutants per commit and, where a defect or a new test could fail first, a red-first run (C7's only
  from the missing known-leak entry): 166 mutants over the eighteen commits, all killed, none judged equivalent; some ran before
  the validation step's last comment-only edits (C1, HF1, HF2, HF3, r1-G2, r2-H3).
- E78 had an independent review in two rounds (security and correctness) with a goal check on part 1. Round 1 read C0 to C3: 2
